diagnostic_evidence.quote: We insist on the fact that for having a fair evaluation of the TTP, in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' (corresponding to the cost $\ell^2$), we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.
At $\tau =0$, set {$u=0$} and keep it constant while $s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)<  1.2\, n_0$ (vacation period).

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines TTP as the first time the tumor reaches 1.2 n0. TTP' is the last time it is at or below that threshold. For the hyperbolic-cost policy and Off-On AT, the tumor is allowed to cross the threshold early and then shrink, so TTP is small while TTP' can be much larger. The paper uses TTP' for these strategies and compares it to TTP of MTD/On-Off AT, which do not cross early. This is not a like-for-like comparison and inflates the apparent time to progression. For Off-On AT, the algorithm explicitly starts with u=0 until n≥1.2 n0, so the first crossing occurs before therapy starts; the reported mean TTP of 306 days for n0=0.5 cannot be the first-crossing TTP.

failure_location.quote: when $\ell$ has a hyperbolic profile, the computed policy suggests a delayed starting of the therapy, and on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression' (see \cref{table:MTD_AT1,table:Sum_Hyp})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-evaluate all delayed-start strategies using the first-crossing TTP defined in eq:def_TTP, or clearly separate the two metrics and avoid claiming TTP improvement when using TTP'. Comparisons must use the same metric for all strategies.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed TTP improvements of the hyperbolic-cost ensemble control and the Off-On AT over MTD and On-Off AT are unsupported. The conclusion that active surveillance can be nearly optimal is based on this inflated metric.
issues.title: Use of TTP' instead of TTP for delayed-start therapies invalidates performance comparisons
issues.why_classification: The central experimental claim of outperformance in time to progression relies on using TTP' instead of TTP for the new strategies. Repairing this requires re-evaluating all strategies and likely withdrawing the claimed TTP advantages, which is a major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \dot r_u^\theta(\tau) = \hat r_R \big( 1 -  r_u^\theta(\tau) \big) r_u^\theta(\tau) - \hat d_T r_u^\theta(\tau)

issues.failure_explanation: On the boundary s=0, the r-dynamics has the form r(\hat r_R(1-r)-\hat d_T). Its zero is at r = 1 - \hat d_T/\hat r_R, not at r = \hat r_R/(\hat r_R+\hat d_T). The stated sign conditions are therefore false when \hat d_T>0. For example, with \hat r_R=1, \hat d_T=0.5 and r=0.6, the derivative is 0.6(0.4-0.5)=-0.06<0, contradicting the first case. The lemma's conclusion is still true, but this proof step is invalid as written.

failure_location.quote: \begin{cases} \dot r_u^\theta(\tau) \geq 0 & \mbox{if } \, 0\leq r_u^\theta(\tau)\leq \frac{\hat r_R}{\hat r_R + \hat d_T},\\ \dot r_u^\theta(\tau) \leq 0 & \mbox{if } \, \frac{\hat r_R}{\hat r_R + \hat d_T} \leq r_u^\theta(\tau)\leq 1, \end{cases}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold with the correct value 1 - \hat d_T/\hat r_R, or remove the unnecessary r-sign analysis since the invariance of the boundary s=0 follows directly from \dot s=0 when s=0.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma domain_invariance contains a false inequality. The lemma itself remains true and can be proven by noting \dot s=0 when s=0 and using the other boundary arguments.
issues.title: Incorrect threshold in boundary invariance proof for $\Delta_1$
issues.why_classification: The error is a local calculation in an unnecessary part of the proof. The lemma's conclusion is unaffected and a short correction restores the proof.
